articles.headline: NFL Week 8 uniforms: Jaguars, Lions become latest team to debut Rivalries look
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 8, led by Rivalries looks from Jacksonville and Detroit.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第8週のユニフォーム：ジャガーズとライオンズが「ライバルリー・ルック」を初披露
articles.descriptionJa: ジャクソンビルとデトロイトを筆頭に、NFL各チームが第8週に着用するユニフォームを紹介します。
articles.body:
The spooky season is here, and the NFL uniforms are looking scary good in Week 8. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Detroit Lions lead the way as they debut their respective Rivalries combinations. 

Jacksonville's look is nicknamed "Bold City," and the team will wear the uniform against the Indianapolis Colts, who debuted their own "Rivalries" design in Week 3. The uniform includes a teal-glossed helmet with a gold face mask and "904," Jacksonville's area code, on the front and "Duuuval," the team's rallying cry, on the back. The white jerseys include black numbers and "Jaguars" in cursive. They both feature gold trimming, while the numbers have a teal shadow and jaguar-print pattern. A similar pattern appears on the black pants, which also have a teal stripe that includes gold trim running down the side. One neat detail is the names of Jacksonville neighborhoods hidden within the spots on the pants. 

Detroit's "Defend the Den" threads will be worn vs. the Minnesota Vikings. The Lions' all-silver combination has various details with a message, including italicized black numbers that lean forward, meant to create the illusion of motion. The shoulder sleeve design of Honolulu blue meeting black mimics the gaze of a lion when it eyes its prey. The same appears as a pant stripe on the uniform's bottom half. And of course, Detroit's iconic car and racing culture are represented. The Honolulu blue lid's Lions decal is in carbon fiber black as a way to connect to that culture.

articles.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 8, which kicks off Thursday night with a game between the Panthers and Packers.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET. 

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

articles.headline: Former Man United midfielder Herrera on City breaches: 'Damage irreparable'
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera is bitter over the EPL title he was deprived of during Manchester City's decade of rules breaching.
articles.headlineJa: 元マン・ユナイテッドのMFヘレラ、シティの違反について「取り返しのつかない損害」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: 元マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのミッドフィールダー、アンデル・ヘレラは、マンチェスター・シティによる長年の規約違反の間に奪われたプレミアリーグのタイトルに対し、憤りを感じている。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera is bitter over the Premier League title that he was deprived of during Manchester City's decade of rules breaching.

Manchester City were last month found guilty on almost all of the 100-plus charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

Herrera, who played for Manchester United from 2014 until 2019 and is now on the books of Real Zaragoza, told the Mario Suárez podcast: "I would have a Premier League title.

"It really changes the picture when you have a Premier League [title]."

There have been calls for Manchester City to be stripped of the three Premier League titles won during the nine-year period. Herrera won four trophies in his five years at Old Trafford but the Premier League was not one of them.

Under José Mourinho, Manchester United finished second, 19 points adrift of City in the 2017-18 campaign.

"It was the year [2018] when Mourinho said that bit about 'I give a lot of credit to this second-place finish because nobody knows what's going on behind the scenes'," Herrera, 37, said.

"Mou [Mourinho]'s like The Simpsons -- whatever he says, it ends up happening. And he'd already been saying that something strange was going on.

"You have to follow the rules, and what was happening wasn't right -- we all realised that. I've had friends who've come to Manchester and they couldn't get tickets to go to Old Trafford, yet the ones for the Etihad were being given away for free. They don't have the fan base, but they spend as if they did..."

Herrera said he sympathises with Manchester City players and staff.

"Nothing to say about the players, nothing to say about the manager [Pep Guardiola]," the Spaniard said. "They deserve all the credit in the world for what they've achieved.

"If I were a Manchester City player, I'd be angry; I'd be furious with those in charge because they've tarnished and cast doubt on everything the team has achieved over the years."

Sanctions have not yet been announced but Herrera agrees with former Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney that the punishment must be significant considering the "irreparable damage" it caused other clubs.

"For me, it has to be something big, something that sets a precedent -- as Rooney said recently," Herrera said.

"It has to set a precedent so that the next person who says, 'I'm going to inflate the revenue illegally' will think, 'No, I won't do it because I'll get relegated.'

"Nottingham Forest were sanctioned [with a four-point deduction in the 2022-23]; Everton were sanctioned [with a 10-point deduction in the 2021-22 season].

"The damage they [Man City] have caused is obviously irreparable.

"In terms of revenue, Tottenham finished fifth for three consecutive years and failed to qualify for the Champions League. That has a significant financial impact on Tottenham."

articles.headline: Bowen: Four players (and a defense) that have changed my mind
articles.description: Matt Bowen discusses a few disappointments, a couple of surprises and what to expect going forward.
articles.headlineJa: ボーウェン：私の考えを変えた4人の選手（とある守備陣）
articles.descriptionJa: マット・ボーウェンが、いくつかの失望、数々の驚き、そして今後の展望について語る。
articles.body:
We're almost at the midpoint of the NFL season, and the fantasy football trade deadline is a little more than a month away. With that in mind, we have seen enough football to highlight some realizations that differ from early-season opinions and expectations.

Yes, there is still a lot of football to be played here, and players can make a quick turnaround if they see a jump in usage or take advantage of a positive matchup. I get that.

But after seven weeks, we can identify the players (and one defensive unit) who have been better or worse than anticipated, and what you can expect going forward.

Justin Jefferson is no longer a clear WR1

I've often called coach Kevin O'Connell's offense one of the more "QB friendly" systems in the league. It's the play design and the defined throws. Scheme guys open. Isolate players in positive matchups. Take shots off play-action. There should be a feeling of tempo and rhythm.

But after watching the Vikings this season -- with Kyler Murray under center -- there is still a genuine lack of identity in the pass game. And we are seeing it even more with Jefferson's declining production.

Jefferson opened the season in Week 1 by dropping 31.2 points on the Green Bay Packers, in a game where Murray left early due to a concussion. Carson Wentz stepped in and Jefferson went on to catch two touchdowns.

But in the three full games Jefferson has played with Murray, he's scoring 10.8 fantasy PPG. Plus, he's averaged 5.3 targets, with only two in the red zone during this three-game stretch. In fact, Jefferson has yet to post a game this season with double-digit targets, and he now plays in a low-volume throwing offense, as the Vikings have attempted only 164 passes this season (second fewest in the league).

Now, I don't expect fantasy managers to give up on Jefferson. There's too much talent and upside despite the recent usage. Plus, Jefferson has some prime matchups over the next two weeks against Detroit and Buffalo, two defenses ranking in the bottom five versus wide receivers. But unless we see a big jump from Murray and the Minnesota pass game, it's fair to question if Jefferson can finish as a top-15 wide receiver by season's end.

Blake Corum is more than just a bye week fill-in

I said the following early in the season on Corum: "Bench stash. Insurance play behind starter Kyren Williams. A running back with some value in deeper formats."

But that has changed given Corum's recent usage and production in the Rams' backfield.

Corum, who saw a team-high 17 carries in the Week 7 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, is scoring 15.8 fantasy PPG over his last three, with double-digit touches and at least one touchdown in each game. Corum has also caught six of seven targets during this stretch, while averaging 77.7 scrimmage yards per game.

articles.headline: Debunk or double down? Judging 10 early-season NBA overreactions
articles.description: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
articles.headlineJa: 間違いか、それとも確信か？シーズン序盤のNBAにおける10の過剰反応を検証
articles.descriptionJa: 29歳の選手がNBAの次なるブレイクスターになる。マイアミのヤニス時代はすでに終わっている。サンダー、ニックス、ウォリアーズも同様だ。どの過剰反応が妥当だろうか？
articles.body:
Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season.

After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as:

The sky is falling in Oklahoma City, New York and Miami!

The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go!

Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball!

Ty Jerome? Ty Jerome!

With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. (Note: stats through Tuesday's games.)

The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008.

Zach Kram: Not an overreaction

For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft.

Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass.

On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo. There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark.

Ben Golliver: Overreaction

Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson, who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo.

Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway. Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist.

articles.headline: Gary Neville tells the Glazers to sell their stakes in Manchester United
articles.description: Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville has told the Glazers "enough is enough" and to sell their stake in the club.
articles.headlineJa: ゲーリー・ネヴィル、グレイザー家にマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの株式売却を要求
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの元キャプテン、ゲーリー・ネヴィルは、グレイザー家に対し「もう十分だ」として、クラブの株式を売却するよう求めた。
articles.body:
Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville has told the Glazers "enough is enough" and to sell their stake in the club.

United are enduring their worst start to a Premier League campaign, while also losing two of their opening three Champions League games, and Michael Carrick is under pressure ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea.

The Glazers, who took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005, remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to Sir Jim Ratcliffe in 2024 and Neville has urged them to leave United completely.

"There's £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they're hamstrung in some ways," Neville said on Stick to Football on Disney+.

"They've spent an absolute fortune on players, just under Man City in the last 15 years. £1.4bn ($1.86bn) on players, they're second in the spending, but a lot of it's the never-never.

"They have to sell now, they have to sell, I'm sorry the time has come.

"They have subcontracted the football department out to INEOS, they are trying to run the football department, they have had three years of struggling and it looks like this year is going to be a struggle.

"The Glazer family over in America, in Tampa, they're very popular over there, they go to every game, apparently, I hear, they go to all the NFL games, they've hardly been to Old Trafford in 20-odd years.

- Man United's Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes hold 'clear-the-air' talks - reports

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Wayne Rooney's son, Kai scores, 4 goals for Man United under-18s vs. Burnley

"My point is, they have to sell now, enough is enough, the club is in debt, you've not spent a penny on the stadium, you're now trying to borrow £2bn for a stadium you don't know how you're going to borrow.

"You've got a failure of 13, 14 years on the football side, you've subbed it out to somebody else, which is ridiculous, and not took responsibility. It is now at a point where they have to sell.

"Enough is enough, they have to sell the whole the club. The fans have had enough. They have to go now."

articles.headlineJa: シャビ・アロンソ：エステヴァンはチェルシーで「見せ場」を迎えるだろう
articles.descriptionJa: チェルシーの指揮官シャビ・アロンソは、まだ172分しか出場していないティーンエイジャーのウィング、エステヴァンについて、今シーズン中に「見せ場」が訪れるだろうと主張している。
articles.body:
Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso insists Estêvão will have "his moment" this season, with the teenage winger having only played 172 minutes.

Estêvão, 19, has started in just two games under head coach Xabi Alonso and was an unused substitute in Chelsea's defeat on penalties to Liverpool in Wednesday's Carabao Cup quarterfinal.

"I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure," Xabi Alonso said in a post-match news conference when asked about the Brazil international's limited playing time.

"Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. We have had some intense games and there will be moments for everything. I'm sure Este [Estêvão] will have his moment. It's my responsibility and we need to deal with that."

Estêvão, who missed the 2026 World Cup through a hamstring injury, made 12 Premier League starts last season and had eight goals in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Seven preseason assumptions already being challenged
articles.description: The fantasy basketball experts go over what hasn't gone as planned during the opening week of the NBA season.
articles.body:
Sometimes, it takes a while to see how the things are going to shake out in this new NBA season. Other times, it is plainly obvious that things are not as they seemed before the season officially tipped off, whether that means less playing time, a drop in production, or changes under a new coaching staff.

With that in mind, we asked our fantasy basketball experts Andre Snellings, Eric Moody, Eric Karabell, Steve Alexander, Jim McCormick and Michael F. Florio to identify the biggest preseason assumptions that are already being challenged.

Here's what has stood out to them after one week of NBA action.

Tyrese Maxey, other 76ers thriving despite Philadelphia's star power

Moody: The concern in Philadelphia was that too many stars would eat into Maxey's production. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown joined Joel Embiid, but Maxey averaged 50 fantasy points per game through four games as the Sixers opened 3-1. Brown contributed 36.0 fantasy points per game, and Embiid recorded a 28-point triple-double against the Milwaukee Bucks last Saturday. There will be nights when someone sacrifices touches, but Maxey hasn't looked like the player making that sacrifice.

Florio: While LeBron and Embiid have already missed a game and that was a big fear, they have performed extremely well so far, especially in Roto formats. Maxey is a Top 5 player in all formats, while Embiid and Brown are each averaging over 20 PPG. LeBron James continues to contribute across the board. It's still early, but fading them in fantasy is one early season regret.

Giannis' arrival is already affecting Adebayo's production

Karabell: Perhaps I hadn't considered the potential statistical downside of what superstar Giannis Antetokoumpo joining the Miami Heat would mean for longtime underrated star Bam Adebayo. So far, the fit looks awkward. Adebayo averaged 20.1 PPG and 10 RPG last season, continuing a seven-season run of excellence. Is that over now? Bam is off to a terrible start (11.8 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 40% FG, 61.5% FT), and oh, Miami is winless. These numbers must improve, but how much? Is Bam still a top 50 fantasy option? Maybe so, maybe not.

Alex Sarr will have to wait to reach new heights

Snellings: Sarr is unlikely to approach, let alone build on, his breakout campaign from last season if the Washington Wizards are fully healthy. After averaging 16.3 PPG, 7.4 RPG and 2.0 BPG last season, he is currently averaging 8.8 PPG, 5.3 RPG and 1.3 BPG in this one. With Anthony Davis occupying all the spaces Sarr prefers but at much higher volume, Sarr just doesn't have the shots (6.5 FGA this season, down from 13.7 FGA last year), rebounding or shot-blocking opportunities to approach what he did last season. And number one overall pick AJ Dybantsa hasn't even played yet this season, so once he's in the fold Sarr may get even fewer looks.

Jabari Smith Jr. is showing signs of another leap

McCormick: I was under the impression that Smith had plateaued as an NBA contributor. It's easy to forget

articles.headline: What has gone wrong for 2025 running backs? Ashton Jeanty, Omarion Hampton, more
articles.description: We thought last year's running back class was going to be great. But Ashton Jeanty, Omarion Hampton, TreVeyon Henderson and others haven't lived up to the hype.
articles.body:
About a year ago, I wrote about the then-rookie class of NFL running backs and how excited I was to see them thriving. During Week 4 of the 2025 season, first-year rookie backs combined to run for 737 yards, the most by any set of rookie rushers during a week of September football since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. It looked like a class that was regarded by prospect mavens as one of the deepest and most compelling groups in recent memory was quickly taking over.

One year later, things aren't looking quite as rosy. In Week 6 of the 2026 season, the class of 2025 combined for just 246 yards on the ground, its collective worst total in any given week so far. With benchings and injuries plaguing so many standouts, the leading rusher from the 2025 class that week was Corey Kiner, an undrafted free agent who was the third-string option on the Patriots. Things were better in Week 7, but the class has collectively topped 600 yards in a single week just once since that big breakout in Week 4 one year ago.

What has gone wrong? Injuries have plagued many of the class' most promising backs. Ashton Jeanty, Ollie Gordon II and LeQuint Allen Jr. are the only three 2025 draft picks at running back to be active in every one of their team's games since entering the league, and Gordon and Allen have been backups for most (or all) of that time. Jeanty has played through several ailments, including an ankle issue that he dealt with this preseason.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Jeanty himself might be a microcosm of the class' struggles as a whole. He entered the league as a highly touted running back out of Boise State, drafted by the Raiders ahead of other offensive options such as tackles Armand Membou, receiver Tetairoa McMillan, tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and tight end Colston Loveland, who were the next four picks off the board. Jeanty has certainly flashed at times over his first year-plus in the league, and there are excuses that can help justify his lack of consistency, but he wouldn't be taken ahead of any of those players if the league took a second shot at the 2025 draft.

I will run through many of the most notable contributors from the 2025 rookie running back class -- Jeanty, Omarion Hampton, Quinshon Judkins, TreVeyon Henderson, Bhayshul Tuten, Cam Skattebo and others -- and deliver a sort of progress update on where they stand. There are certainly success stories, but they're coming from surprising places. And while their final NFL story is far from written, it's fair to start wondering whether we'll see some of the most promising and highly touted backs from 2025 live up to what we saw from them as rookies, let alone as prospects.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany discharged from hospital after collapse
articles.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from the hospital following his collapse last week.
articles.headlineJa: バイエルンのヴィンセント・コンパニー、倒れた後に退院
articles.descriptionJa: バイエルンのヴィンセント・コンパニー監督は、先週の失神を受けて病院を退院しました。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was discharged from hospital on Wednesday following his collapse last week.

The Bundesliga champions' director of sport Max Eberl told German broadcaster ARD that Kompany, 40, had been diagnosed with meningeal irritation after being admitted to hospital on Friday.

- Bayern honor Kane for Ballon d'Or win before German Cup rout

Eberl was speaking before Bayern's 6-1 thrashing of Magdeburg in the German Cup at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night, five days after Kompany had collapsed while watching the club's second team train.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing ⁠well," Eberl said. "He ‌was discharged from the hospital [on Wednesday]. That is the biggest and best news for all of ‌us.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication and I am certain that he will ⁠very soon be back on the touchline, operating at 100 percent."

Eberl had said on Friday that it would be "weeks, not days" before the Belgian coach, who had been ill with a virus, would be able to return to work.

Harry Kane revealed after his Ballon d'Or win in London on Monday night that Kompany had telephoned him to wish him luck earlier that morning.

Kompany missed Saturday's 3-1 Bundesliga win at Freiburg, with assistant Aaron Danks taking charge of the ⁠team for that match and the cup win over Magdeburg.

Bayern are top of the Bundesliga table on goal difference, level on points with Borussia Dortmund who they play at home on Saturday.

Information from PA contributed to this report.
